name: Missouri

default_limits.basis: RSMo § 304.010 (eff. 8/28/2026): 75 rural interstates/freeways, 65 rural expressways, 60 urbanized-area interstates/freeways/expressways, 60 other roads outside urbanized areas, 55 max on lettered two-lane state roads; unmarked county roads in 2nd-4th class counties 50. Cities set their own limits by ordinance (no statewide residential default).

fine.notes: Set by local court/violations-bureau schedules; statewide schedule not found. Range from one municipal schedule (Arnold, 2022): $50.50 (1-5 over) to $155.50 (20-25 over); 26+ must appear. Max $750 (class C misd.).

court_costs.notes: Varies by court. Example: Arnold municipal $30.50. State-charge circuit costs not verified.

points.notes: 3 points for speeding under state law; 2 points if charged under a city/county ordinance (RSMo § 302.302).

court.reason: 20+ over is a class B misdemeanor; many courts require appearance (e.g. 26+ in Arnold).

arrest.offense: Speeding 20+ mph over posted limit (class B misdemeanor); under 20 over is class C misdemeanor (max 15 days, $750)
arrest.license: No automatic suspension found; points accrue.

sources.title: Arnold, MO violations bureau schedule (municipal example)
MO Supreme Court order on uniform fine schedule (2018)
News: 75 mph law takes effect 8/28/2026, MoDOT studying (secondary)

notes: All Missouri speeding is a misdemeanor; 20+ over is class B (6 mo/$1,000). NEW 8/28/2026: rural interstate max 75, but MoDOT is still studying and most signs remain 70 for now - trust posted limit. Fines/costs vary by court (low confidence). Points taken from 2026 bill text of § 302.302, not the code page.
